Trigger 4 (Reform regains lead across 3+ houses, or Farage wins Clacton on high turnout with share materially above 73 percent): DID NOT FIRE. Only Freshwater has Reform ahead. question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
key_change: Hold at 85 percent, with the lower bound tightened one point to 72. The 12-13 August window produced substantial infrastructure news but no capability or declaration news that moves the resolution bar. Dated items. (1) The Goodheart Labs AGI Timelines Dashboard, read 13 Aug 2026, shows a combined median of 2031 with an 80 percent interval of 2027-2043. That is the same median as the 8 Aug stamp with the upper bound in by roughly a year, from 2044 to 2043. Marginally supportive, within noise. Underlying components: Metaculus full four-condition median January 2033, weakly-general median June 2028, Kalshi OpenAI-AGI-by-2030 near 55 percent, Polymarket 2027 near 9 percent. (2) ARC Prize verified data refreshed 12 Aug 2026 still shows Claude Opus 5 (High) top of ARC-AGI-3 at 30.2 percent, unchanged since 24 July, with GPT-5.6 Sol far back at 7.8 percent. (3) Nvidia announced on 10 Aug memoranda of understanding with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to mobilise over 500 billion dollars of third-party capital for AI compute financing, with Huang framing GPUs as an investable asset class; coverage ran through 11 Aug (Nvidia newsroom, CNBC 10 Aug, CNN and Fortune 11 Aug). (4) TSMC reported July revenue of NT$467.58bn, up 44.7 percent year on year, and raised 2026 capex guidance to 60-64 billion dollars (CNBC, 10 Aug). (5) Google DeepMind leadership reshuffle confirmed 12 Aug, Kavukcuoglu taking operational control, Hassabis to chairman, Jeff Dean departing (CNBC, 12 Aug). (6) Anthropic disclosed roughly 71 billion dollars of SPV chip-lease compute commitments in the same week. TRIGGER CHECK. Trigger 1 (ARC-AGI-3 base model materially above 30.2 percent): DID NOT FIRE. Leaderboard static, verified 12 Aug. Trigger 2 (OpenAI S-1 public on EDGAR showing self-funding capex through 2030): DID NOT FIRE. The S-1 remains confidential since the 8 June submission and had not surfaced on EDGAR as of 9 Aug; reported financials point the other way, with gross margin near 39 percent in Q1 2026 and cash burn around 27bn in 2026 rising to roughly 63bn in 2027. Trigger 3 (reproducible AI-self-directed research gains, or 2+ leading researchers declaring AGI): DID NOT FIRE, but it is the nearest miss. OpenAI's stated goal of an automated research intern by September 2026 is now weeks away, TIME ran a 7 Aug piece on the recursive self-improvement race at OpenAI and Anthropic, and Karpathy's AutoResearch agent ran 700 experiments and surfaced 20 training improvements. None of that is a lab-published reproducible capability gain, and no second researcher has joined Huang's March 2026 claim. Trigger 4 (Goodheart median past 2033 or upper past 2046): DID NOT FIRE, both moved the other way. Trigger 5 (financing failure, cancellation, GPU credit default): DID NOT FIRE, and the week ran the opposite direction, though the Nvidia structure is MOU only and subject to definitive agreements. Trigger 6 (binding verified international compute thresholds): DID NOT FIRE, proposals only. Judgement. Capital supply firmed materially and capability measurement did not move. Offsetting this, METR judged GPT-5.6 Sol's time horizon unmeasurable because of record benchmark gaming, and 30-50 percent of US 2026 data centre projects are now expected delayed or cancelled. Compute abundance is a necessary but slow-acting input to a 2035 horizon that is already generously long, so the marginal information value is small. Hold.

question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
key_change: HOLD at 7 percent central, with the 80 percent CI narrowed marginally from [4, 12] to [4, 11]. No trigger fired, and the single live near-term uncertainty resolved on the benign side. Dated items in the window. (1) The China-Indonesia drill east of Taiwan, announced by the PRC MND on 11 August, concluded on the morning of 12 August, per the PLA Eastern Theater Command via Global Times (12 Aug) and Xinhua (12 Aug). Content was minimal: maritime communications, formation manoeuvring, replenishment at sea, and a farewell ceremony between the Type 054A frigate Honghe (Hull 523) and Indonesia's KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai. (2) On 12 August the Indonesian Navy publicly reframed it as a routine passing exercise conducted while the ship transited home from a visit to Russia via Japan, spokesman Tunggul saying it was a universal naval tradition and not related to war fighting (Reuters, via Taipei Times front page 13 Aug). (3) Taiwan's assistant deputy chief of the general staff for intelligence, Major General Wu Tien-jen, told the legislature on 12 August that the Indonesian ship was 70 to 80 nautical miles off Taiwan's east coast and that militarily this does not have a direct impact on Taiwan, only geopolitical significance. (4) Taiwan's MAC on 11-12 August called it a military provocation and exercises in name, expansion in fact. (5) Sortie counts: 9 Aug 4 aircraft and 6 PLAN vessels; 11 Aug 2 aircraft, 7 PLAN and 6 official ships; 12 Aug 6 aircraft and 8 PLAN with 4 median-line crossings; 13 Aug 18 aircraft, 11 PLAN and 3 official ships with 15 of 18 crossing the median line into the northern, central, southwestern and eastern ADIZ (Taiwan MND via ANI/Tribune, 13 Aug). (6) Beidaihe readout (Taipei Times, 11 Aug): four Taiwan priorities set, including backing patriotic forces in the 28 November local elections and blocking a new phase of US arms sales to avoid disrupting the current strategic layout ahead of Xi's 24 September Washington visit. TRIGGER CHECK. Trigger 1 (traffic control without weather or safety pretext, or CCG boarding a Taiwan-bound commercial ship): DID NOT FIRE. The Guangdong MSA order carried an explicit Typhoon Dolphin pretext, which Taipei and the US State Department (11 Aug) called pretextual but which is a weather pretext on the trigger's own terms. The nearest incident, CCG 2304 tailing the Japan Coast Guard's Urado on 7 August, involved a government vessel, no boarding, no commercial ship. Trigger 2 (Indonesia drill expanded, extended, or followed by a further third-country or named PLA drill within 30 days): DID NOT FIRE, and moved the opposite way. It lasted under a day, was smaller than billed, and Jakarta distanced itself. Trigger 3 (ADIZ incursions at 2024-25 norms for two consecutive months, or a Joint Sword / Strait Thunder pattern exercise announced): DID NOT FIRE. The 13 August figure is a one-day Han Kuang-timed spike from a depressed base and sits at or below 2024-25 daily norms; no named exercise announced. Trigger 4 (Han Kuang concludes clean plus summit reassurance): NOT YET RESOLVED, Han Kuang 42 ends 14 August and the summit is 24 September. Trigger 5 (November election): NOT YET RESOLVED, though Polymarket has KMT around 84 percent. What drove the judgement: two mild downward signals (benign resolution of the drill, Beidaihe prioritising elections and the summit) offset one mild upward signal (the ETC and Zhang Junshe framing the drill as proof of PRC sovereign rights and jurisdiction over the EEZ east of Taiwan, which is legal groundwork for quarantine). Net zero on the central.

question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
key_change: No change. Central holds at 1% with an 80% CI of [0, 2]. Nothing in the 12-13 August window moved the arithmetic, and what did move leaned marginally against YES. TRIGGER CHECK. Trigger 1 (July CPI at or below 2.2% on 19 August) DID NOT FIRE: the print is still six days away, so it cannot yet resolve. The pre-print evidence is unhelpful for YES. Petrol hit a new Iran-War high of 160.85p a litre in August with diesel back above 180p for the first time since 9 June, and the RAC sees diesel heading toward 185p (petrolprices.co.uk, August 2026). Motor fuels contributed 0.6pp to June's 2.6% and were falling then; they were rising through July. Trigger 2 (Hormuz deal plus Brent held below $70 and NBP under about 100p/therm) DID NOT FIRE, and moved further away. Brent opened at $88.98 on 12 August and traded around $89.26, up 0.33% (Forbes Advisor, Fortune, 12 Aug). Trump claimed on 12 August that the US has 'total control' of the Strait and hinted he wants to 'KEEP' it; Tehran rejected the claim outright and an IRGC adviser said Iran could 'prolong' the war until Trump leaves office (CNN, ABC live blogs, 12 Aug). CNBC's 11 August piece was headlined 'Hormuz deadlock', with Iran insisting the US naval blockade must lift first. The IEA on 12 August cut its 2026 demand forecast by a further 510,000 b/d to a 1.6m b/d decline and warned global stocks are drawing rapidly (CNBC, 12 Aug). NBP gas was around 143p/therm on 12 August (Trading Economics), well above the 100p threshold. Trigger 3 (October cap CUT on like-for-like TDCV, or a BoE 17 September downgrade below 2.5%) DID NOT FIRE. Cornwall Insight's 22 July prediction, calculated on 21 July closes and already including the electricity VAT cut, puts October-December at £1,699.58 on new TDCVs versus the £1,663 July cap, and £1,906.27 on the old TDCVs versus £1,862. That is a rise of roughly 2.2-2.4%, not a cut. The BoE decision is five weeks out. Trigger 4 (Brent sustained above $90 for a week-plus with talks formally collapsed, or NBP above 160p) DID NOT FIRE, but only just: Brent is $89 and sitting below $90, talks are stalled rather than formally collapsed, and NBP at 143p is below 160p. Trigger 5 (July or August CPI at or above 3.0%, or cap materially above like-for-like £1,899) DID NOT FIRE: no print yet, and £1,906.27 is 0.4% above the £1,899 reference, which is not material. Two dated items added mild downward pressure on YES. Houthi militants killed six in a strike on the Tanzania-flagged Tihamah in Bab el-Mandeb on 12 August, the first fatal attack there in a year, on top of a declared blockade that cut transits to eleven vessels a day (Al Jazeera, Semafor, The Hill, 12 Aug). And today's ONS release showed Q2 GDP up 0.4% q/q with June monthly GDP at +0.3%, above expectations, and household consumption up 0.3% (Bloomberg, FXStreet, 13 Aug). A resilient economy removes the demand-collapse route to sub-2%. The Commons Library economic update, revised 12 August, restates the BoE July MPR central path of 3.2% in October and November and above 3% until Q3 2027. With services inflation at 3.6% in June and only July to November reference months publishable before 1 January, the gap to a sub-2.0% print is not closable.

question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
key_change: Hold at 100 (rounded; treated as >99.9%, not literal certainty). The bar has been cleared by a wide and still-widening margin, and today's check confirms the figure moved up, not down. Verified current figure: The Numbers, retrieved 13 August 2026, shows Worldwide Box Office $1,708,805,242, composed of Domestic $691,066,077 (cumulative through Tuesday 11 August, day 12) and International $1,017,739,165 (territory report date 8/12/2026). Headroom above the $1,500,000,000 bar is $208,805,242, or 13.9% of the current total. Yesterday's reading was $1,688,767,811, so the page added $20,037,431 overnight, entirely from the newly posted domestic daily for Tuesday 11 August ($20.04M, +20% on Monday's $16.69M). These are client-side-rendered or stale server-cached pages, not evidence of a removed or restated record. TRIGGER CHECK. (1) DOWN only if BOTH BOM and The Numbers restate below $1.5B: NOT TRIGGERED. The Numbers restated upward by $20.0M; a fall below the bar would now require a 12.2% cut. (2) DOWN slightly if a resolving source removes the page, flags data as disputed, or announces a methodology change: NOT TRIGGERED. The Numbers page is live, complete, carries an OpusData ID (709940100), and shows no dispute flag or methodology notice. BOM's non-retrieval is a rendering limitation affecting all its pages, not a page removal specific to this title. (3) Flag for review if BOM's directly retrieved worldwide total differs from The Numbers by more than 3%: CANNOT BE EVALUATED, as BOM's aggregate remains unretrievable; the third-party aggregate that blends BOM data agrees to within 0.1%. (4) No upward revision possible; already at ceiling. This is effectively a resolved observation rather than a forecast: the event has occurred and been recorded, and the remaining probability mass sits entirely on data-integrity failure at both resolving sources.

question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
key_change: No move. Central stays 99%, CI [98, 99]. The 12-13 August window produced a dense news flow but nothing that touches the resolution mechanics in either direction, while the fundamentals underneath quietly got stronger. Dated items in the window. On 11 August OpenAI completed its $7bn employee tender at an unchanged $852bn valuation (CNBC 10 Aug, Yahoo Finance, Qz, Dataconomy 11 Aug); several outlets read tender completion as a signal that a listing is not immediately imminent. Also 11 August, Bloomberg, TechCrunch, CNBC, Axios and Fortune reported COO Brad Lightcap is leaving after nine years, with ex-CPO Kevin Weil raising $150m for an AI-for-science startup (Business Insider) - a leadership thinning, not a revenue event. On 12 August the WSJ reported Anthropic is meeting potential investors to shore up confidence ahead of a planned September or early-October IPO, with investors pressing on cheap Chinese models, Trump administration friction and data-centre opposition; Anthropic told some investors it will push into healthcare and biology. Also 12 August, Anthropic, Macquarie Asset Management and GIC announced Theseus Infrastructure, a purpose-built data-centre platform majority-funded by Macquarie and GIC with Anthropic absorbing consumer electricity price increases (Bloomberg 10 Aug, Macquarie release, DCD). On 10 August Riot Platforms disclosed a 20-year, 191 MW Rockdale lease that Bloomberg identifies as Anthropic, worth about $9.1bn base and up to $16.1bn with extensions. No named outlet published a fresh ARR print for either firm on 12 or 13 August. Fundamentals that firmed. TickerTrends' July update has Anthropic $74.1bn and OpenAI $41.3bn, with OpenAI accelerating from $33.0bn in May to $41.3bn in July and Anthropic's month-over-month growth cooling from roughly 55% in spring to mid-single digits. CFO Sarah Friar told OpenAI staff on 29 July that July annualized revenue topped all of Q2, credited to GPT-5.6, ChatGPT Work and Codex (CNBC, Reuters). That kills the 'OpenAI flat since February' framing in the prior status note. WSJ has Anthropic Q2 recognised revenue at $10.9bn, up from $4.8bn in Q1, with a first operating profit near $559m; SemiAnalysis (8 Jul) states the two 'combine for ~$100B of ARR' today and models Anthropic above $60bn ARR by Q3. TRIGGER CHECK. 1 (Anthropic public S-1 restates net below $47bn): DID NOT FIRE. No public S-1 on EDGAR from either firm as of 13 Aug; the gross-versus-net question remains open and only in SEC review. 2 (named outlet reports MoM decline, or combined below $70bn): DID NOT FIRE. Deceleration in growth rate is reported, but no decline and no sub-$70bn combined figure anywhere. 3 (OpenAI formally defers to 2027 AND Anthropic slips past Q4): DID NOT FIRE, and is now half-refuted - WSJ on 12 Aug has Anthropic aiming at September or early October. The tender completion is a weak deferral hint at most. 4 (qualifying Q4 print for both above $70bn): DID NOT FIRE, which is exactly why the estimate cannot go above 99. 5 (EDGAR monitoring): nothing public yet; OpenAI's prospectus is still expected mid-to-late August. The judgement: the bar is now cleared several times over on almost any accounting basis, including a punitive net restatement of Anthropic. The only live failure mode is a reporting vacuum, and the Anthropic roadshow plus OpenAI's expected prospectus both cut against it.

question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
key_change: Move: 33% to 34%, CI [20,47] to [21,48]. A one-point nudge up. The explicit DOWN trigger for today did not fire, and the balance of dated news in the 12-13 August window was marginally constructive on the demand side while unchanged to slightly worse on the supply side. The actual print. ONS published the GDP first quarterly estimate for April to June 2026 at 07:00 on Thursday 13 August 2026. UK real GDP rose 0.4% q/q in Q2 2026, exactly in line with the Bloomberg consensus of +0.4%, after +0.6% in Q1. Annual growth was 1.2% y/y against 1.1% expected and 0.9% in Q1. The monthly series was the surprise: June came in at +0.3% m/m against a consensus of 0.0% and Pantheon's -0.1%, May was revised down from +0.1% to 0.0%, and April was unrevised at -0.1%. Composition: services +0.5% (information and communication +2.7%, professional/scientific/technical +1.7%), production flat, construction +0.3%. Expenditure side: gross fixed capital formation +1.2%, household consumption +0.3%, government consumption -0.3%. June industrial production was -0.2% m/m and manufacturing -0.5% m/m. Liz McKeown of ONS said growth 'slowed in the second quarter of the year, following a strong start to 2026, but remained relatively robust'. Chancellor John Healey claimed 'the fastest growth in the G7 this year'. Schroders' George Brown and KPMG's Yael Selfin both flagged that the men's World Cup and repeated heatwaves flattered June and that momentum should fade. Other dated items. The 10-year gilt held at 4.98% on 13 August, up from 4.92% on 11 August, near two-decade highs on term premium. GBP/USD was flat at 1.3495 despite the beat. Brent was around $89-90 and up 6% on the week as Hormuz talks stalled; Treasury officials have warned PM Andy Burnham that GDP grows only about 0.3% next year if the strait stays blocked to end-2026, and the BoE has said it would hike in that scenario. Bank Underground published on 6 August finding AI productivity gains concentrated in AI-producing sectors (computer programming and consultancy lifting its contribution from 0.01pp to 0.10pp) rather than adopters. Treasury is reportedly scoping over £9bn a year of extra capital borrowing by 2031 via the fiscal-rule asset offset, routed through the National Wealth Fund, National Housing Bank, British Business Bank and mayors. TRIGGER CHECK. (1) UP on potential growth upgrade or AI broadening: DID NOT FIRE. IMF July 2026 Article IV still puts potential at 1.4%; OBR is briefed to cut trend productivity a further 0.1-0.2pp at the 28 October forecast; the BoE evidence shows AI gains narrow, not broadening. (2) UP on gilts below 4% or capex recovery: DID NOT FIRE. Gilt 4.98%; BCC Q2 QES investment intentions fell to 17%, a post-pandemic low, versus the 25% threshold, with BCC forecasting business investment -2.2% in 2026. (3) DOWN on Q2 at or below +0.2% or negative June: DID NOT FIRE. Q2 was +0.4% and June +0.3%. (4) DOWN on gilts above 5.5% or capital-led consolidation: DID NOT FIRE. Budget now looks like £22-25bn of tax rises alongside protected or expanded capital borrowing. (5) DOWN on Hormuz into 2027 above $100 Brent or AI displacement without productivity: PARTIALLY BUILDING, not fired. Brent below $100; but UK job postings are down 11% year to date, graduate postings at a post-pandemic low and youth unemployment 16.2%, against output per hour up only 0.4% y/y. Judgement: one in-line quarter tells you almost nothing about a decade average fourteen years out. It rules out the tail where 2026 collapses outright, worth about 1pp. The structural arithmetic is unchanged: roughly 1% trend productivity plus roughly 0.4% labour supply leaves potential near 1.4%, still just below the bar.
